# Vendored `osqp`

`osqp_patched.mjs` is `osqp@0.0.2` with one defect fixed: the published package
leaks WebAssembly heap on every solve, and its heap is fixed at 16 MiB and
aborts rather than grows. That capped a portfolio optimizer run at 36 solves at
N=100 against a default plan of 56; the rest fell back to the pure-JavaScript
solver, roughly an order of magnitude slower, with no user-visible signal beyond
the run taking longer.

The package is unmaintained — `0.0.2` is `latest`, published 2022-05-12 — and
the leak cannot be fixed from application code, because the Emscripten module is
closure-private and `_free` is unreachable from outside the bundle.

**Do not edit this file by hand.** It is generated:

```
node tools/optimizer/patch_osqp.mjs --write
```

`tools/optimizer/patch_osqp.mjs` carries the four exact edits and the full
rationale. `tools/optimizer/patch_osqp.test.mjs` re-runs the transform against
the installed package on every `npm run check`, so a stale copy or an upstream
change fails the build rather than silently reinstating the leak. It also
asserts that every `shadow-cljs.edn` build resolves `"osqp"` here.

If a future `osqp` release fixes this upstream, delete this directory, drop the
`:js-options` resolves, and let the package resolve normally. One of the tests
above exists to prompt exactly that.
